Class TenantHoldRebuildRunner

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.repository.helper.TenantHoldRebuildRunner
public final class TenantHoldRebuildRunner extends Object
Runs a hold table rebuild for every tenant so that one tenant's data cannot cost every other tenant its rebuild.

The rebuild of all tenants used to be a single transaction around a loop, and the per-tenant method was reached by a self-invocation that never passed the transactional proxy. A single corrupt row therefore rolled back the rebuild of every tenant and, because the exception left RebuildHolingAllTenantOrSingleTask.doWork immediately, the hold tables that would have been rebuilt afterwards were not touched at all. Corrupt data does occur — a cash transfer whose con_id_transaction points at its own row is not forbidden by any database constraint — so the failure is isolated to the tenant that carries it.

The rebuild is still reported as failed: the caller receives one exception naming every tenant that could not be rebuilt, which shows up in the task administration. What changes is that the healthy tenants keep their fresh rows and the failed ones keep the rows they had, because each tenant commits or rolls back on its own.

  • Method Details

    • rebuildPerTenant

      public static void rebuildPerTenant(List<Integer> idTenants, Consumer<Integer> rebuildTenant, String table)
      Rebuilds one hold table tenant by tenant, continuing after a failure.
      Parameters:
      idTenants - the tenants to rebuild, in processing order
      rebuildTenant - the per-tenant rebuild, which must be invoked through the repository proxy so that its own @Transactional takes effect and a failure rolls back that tenant alone
      table - the hold table being rebuilt, used in the log and in the summarising exception
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if at least one tenant could not be rebuilt
